data.narrative:
Fractile is a Series B semiconductor company that has raised $220M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 11 private-stage frontier semiconductor firms (including Positron AI, SambaNova Systems, d-Matrix, and DEEPX) and 3 public semiconductor benchmarks (ALAB, NVDA, AMD), though public comps cannot be anchored due to lack of disclosed revenue.

Two quantitative methods apply. Stage-progression analysis, using the $220M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, implies $418M. Peer-median anchoring across the four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields $1.5B, with a range of $529M to $11.0B. Public-comp P/S anchoring (median 21.0x across semiconductors) is inapplicable without revenue disclosure. The triangulation of these two methods produces a low of $355M, a median of $959M, and a high of $1.7B.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $355M to $1.7B, with a midpoint near $960M. Key uncertainties include stage timing (Series B companies show high valuation dispersion), capital efficiency relative to the peer cohort, and the extreme outlier valuation of SambaNova Systems at $11.0B, which inflates the peer range substantially. Revenue or unit-economics disclosure would enable P/S-based triangulation and tighten the estimate.
